body:
`person:group-pc-jeweller` · flag: **poor** · confidence: verified · tickers: PCJEWELLER

Flag: POOR (history) with an in-progress balance-sheet repair. 2018: the stock fell ~70%+ after a proposed buyback was withdrawn, promoters' related selling surfaced and questions arose on inventory, export receivables and a promoter-family 'gift' of shares. SEBI's final order (May-2021) fined four individuals and an entity Rs 1 cr in total and barred them for one year for insider trading around the 2018 buyback/capital announcements, including Rs 20 lakh on MD Balram Garg for communicating UPSI; the Supreme Court (Apr-2022) set aside SEBI/SAT orders against Garg's relatives (and, per reports, related findings) on the 'connected person' presumption -- regulator findings did not survive appeal. 2019-2023: export receivables and inventory problems, lender defaults; SBI-led consortium of 14 banks moved recovery/insolvency proceedings. Sep-2024 one-time settlement with the consortium; by 2026 filings the company reported repaying all 14 banks and receiving no-dues and release of mortgaged assets (verify against exchange filings). Funding of the turnaround included large preferential warrant issues to promoter/investors, heavy equity dilution, and a stock that rose many-fold from 2023 lows on the settlement narrative. Investor read: debt repaired, but history of insider-trading allegations, receivable write-offs and dilution means the governance record is not repaired by debt repayment alone; watch receivables recovery, inventory audit and promoter allotment pricing.

- **regulator findings:** SEBI 2021 insider-trading order (partly set aside by SC 2022)
- **good conduct:** bank debt OTS repaid by 2026 (company filings)

Sources:

- **False rejects:** Titan (5-year CFO/PAT 0.62, under our 0.7 cut-off), Apollo Hospitals (pledge >25%) and HAL (receivables and negative CFO).
- **False pass:** Vakrangee, whose CFO exceeded PAT in FY17-18. Only the "numbers too good for the business" test and the auditor exit caught it.
- **Proposal (for the user to decide):** keep the hard disqualifiers. Turn the soft flags (P/E, FCF, debt, receivables, pledge) into graded flags that need a written override row. Track false alarms and missed traps every quarter.

Reading: the "beats IWM" numbers are entirely explained by the size/survivor profile of the firms —
the random size-matched controls beat IWM by the same ~1.7%/yr (they are survivors and mid-cap-tilted).
Versus SPY the events lost badly because 2021–2025 was a mega-cap decade, not because of the signal.
Mean > median throughout: a few big winners, most events lag. That skew is the classic small-cap lottery shape.

body:
- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:TVSMOTOR:q4fy27-volume-growth-15pct-plus`
- **Method:** sector cycle/lead indicator · **P(ours)** 0.45 · **P(base)** 0.55 · resolve by 2027-04-15
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (Nov-2026): Q2 volume 1.9 mn vs 1.5 mn (+27%); revenue +44%; domestic ICE 2W +16% vs industry +10%; 2W exports +33%; EV 2W +129%; 3W +47%. Management: 'You will see much higher growth from TVS in quarter 3 and quarter 4.' Macro: repo hikes, El Niño rural stress, high fuel prices; Jan–Mar 2026 base is elevated by the post-GST-cut demand surge.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Share gains and exports are real, but the base quarter (Jan–Mar 2026) was strong and the rate/rural cycle is turning against two-wheelers. Lean slightly below base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** For a company growing ~25% in the latest quarter, the chance of ≥15% two quarters later is ~55% (growth mean-reverts).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if the sum of TVS Motor's reported total sales (2W + 3W, domestic + exports, incl. EV) for Jan, Feb and Mar 2027 ÷ the same sum for Jan–Mar 2026 − 1 ≥ 15.0%, per TVS monthly sales press releases.
- **Resolution source:** TVS Motor monthly sales press releases (NSE announcements), Jan–Mar 2027
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/TVSMOTOR_04112026174008_NSEBSEInvestorcalltranscript.pdf

body:
- O_bk: 8-K with item 1.03 (bankruptcy/receivership) filed in window (SEC submissions, all pages).
- O_delist: delisting for cause = 8-K item 3.01 in window **and** a Form 25 / 25-NSE / 15 in window **and no merger
  evidence** in window (8-K item 5.01, DEFM14A/DEFM14C/PREM14A, SC 14D9, SC TO-T, SC 13E3, 425).
- O_px: lowest month-end adjusted close in window ≤ 0.2 × adjusted close on the last trading day ≤ T (Yahoo v8).
- **O_fail = O_bk ∨ O_delist ∨ O_px** (primary). Firms without usable Yahoo history can fail only via EDGAR events;
  how many there are, and their EDGAR fate (acquired / bankrupt / delisted / went dark / alive), is audited.
  Secondary **O_strict = O_bk ∨ O_delist** (pure EDGAR, fully survivorship-free). Sensitivity: primary metrics on
  firms with full price history or an EDGAR failure event only.
- 5-year total return R5 = adj close at last trading day ≤ T+5y ÷ adj close at T (missing if the series ends > 10 days
  early or Yahoo identity check fails: unadjusted close at T × shares (latest dei cover value ≤ T) must be within
  0.4–8 × float). **Winner** = R5 > 3. Size-matched excess for flag F = R5 − median R5 of F-unflagged firms in the same
  snapshot and float quintile.
